items.title: A multimodal tool-augmented agent for evidence-based clinical decision support in longitudinal AMD follow-up
items.excerpt: An AI agent combines retinal imaging findings across visits to support decisions on disease activity and anti-VEGF injection intervals in age-related macular degeneration, work that is time-consuming to do by hand.

items.title: AI-driven multi-horizon risk stratification for heart failure hospitalization in UA with HFpEF: a Chinese multi-center cohort study
items.excerpt: Multicenter Chinese cohort: AI model stratifies short- and long-horizon heart-failure hospitalization risk in HFpEF patients with unstable angina.

items.title: As more doctors consult chatbots, health systems can block them — or buy in
items.excerpt: As hundreds of thousands of doctors consult AI chatbots to make care decisions, health systems weigh blocking them versus licensing HIPAA-compliant versions. (STAT+ paywall; body may be partial.)

items.title: FDA, CMS look to collaborate with states on health AI
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech: federal officials look to work with states on regulating clinical AI and protecting doctors from AI liability. (STAT+ paywall.)

items.title: How should the FDA regulate generative AI in medtech? Here are 5 takes
items.excerpt: Patients, providers and medtech firms filed hundreds of comments on FDA's approach to generative AI in medical devices; five positions summarized.

items.title: Patients want a human in the loop for AI healthcare tools
items.excerpt: Survey of 3,488 U.S. adults: patients accept AI for admin tasks like jargon translation and scheduling when a human reviews output, but not for diagnosis or claims adjudication.

items.title: 7 Potential Problems with Medicare's AI Prior Authorization Experiment
items.excerpt: CMS documents obtained by EFF via FOIA lawsuit detail early problems in the WISeR model, where six tech companies use AI to review Medicare prior authorization requests in six states.

items.title: AI Didn't Reduce Clinician Burden — It Just Moved It
items.excerpt: Opinion: AI documentation tools solve a visible pain point, but the burden of reviewing and editing AI output shifts work rather than removing it. (Opinion piece; weak unless paired with data.)

items.title: 병원 문턱 넘은 병리 AI…수가와 디지털 전환 비용은 숙제
items.excerpt: Pathology AI in Korean hospitals is shifting from read-assist to treatment-response prediction (e.g., AZ/Daiichi TROP2 biomarker phase 3), but sustained use hinges on reimbursement and digital-conversion costs; demonstrations must feed into benefit evaluation.

items.title: 동탄시티병원, AI로 재택환자 위험 조기 발견…병원·지역사회 잇는 통합돌봄 구축
items.excerpt: 180-bed Dongtan City Hospital, which runs AI for imaging, surgery/rehab and ward monitoring plus a command center, outlined an AI home-care model that flags health changes in homebound patients and routes them to home visits or admission.

items.title: 루닛, 미국면역항암학회서 랩콥·셀카르타와 AI 활용 연구성과 공개
items.excerpt: At SITC 2026 Lunit presents Lunit SCOPE IO studies with Labcorp and Cellcarta: H&E-only AI HRD score in 339 ovarian cancer patients correlated with genomic instability score, informing PARP-inhibitor selection.

items.title: Radiology residents miss more findings after night shifts, even with AI assistance
items.excerpt: A new analysis finds radiology residents miss more findings after overnight shifts and that AI assistance did not fully compensate for fatigue-related diagnostic errors.

items.title: AI recommends vastly more expensive treatment than physicians, analysis suggests
items.excerpt:
Artificial intelligence (AI) systems suggest medical tests and treatment plans that are more than three times as expensive as those recommended by doctors, a study has found.1

items.title: FDA clears Deep Reasoning AI's neurovascular CTA software
items.excerpt: Deep Reasoning AI received FDA 510(k) clearance for NeuroDR, which runs automatically after a head-and-neck CTA, removes bone, soft tissue and veins, and sends 3D vessel reconstructions to PACS.

items.title: Parent Comfort With Artificial Intelligence-Led Behavioral Therapy for Their Child
items.excerpt: Boston Children's survey of 572 US parents: 76% not comfortable with AI-led behavioral therapy for their child; comfort strongly tied to parents' own comfort with AI therapy (aOR 20.9).

items.title: AI-Identified Reasons for Nonescalation of Lipid-Lowering Therapy for Secondary Prevention
items.excerpt: Large language models read clinical notes for 28,113 patients with ASCVD: among 13,810 with above-goal LDL-C, therapy was not escalated in 88.7% of relevant notes, and 40.4% of those documented a reason, most often patient-reported adverse effects (12.6%), LDL-C near goal (6.9%) and patient preference (6.8%).

items.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Scribe for Clinical Notes
items.excerpt: NEJM Clinical Decisions feature (Nov. 4 issue) on using an AI scribe to write clinical notes. Body not retrievable (403); excerpt based on title and Crossref metadata only - enrichment should verify.

items.title: Performance of artificial intelligence versus clinician left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI for mortality prediction: a retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study
items.excerpt: In 27,382 UK and US patients followed for more than five years (3,458 deaths), AI-derived ejection fraction from cardiac MRI predicted mortality slightly but significantly better than clinician measurements; the AI analysed each scan in about 2-3 seconds versus roughly 13 minutes for an expert (City St George's / UCL).

items.title: False Reassurances from False Negatives: AI Stroke Algorithms and Their Anatomical Blind Spots
items.excerpt: Radiology: Artificial Intelligence piece (Nov. 4) on false-negative results from AI stroke-detection algorithms and their anatomical blind spots. Body not retrievable (Cloudflare); excerpt based on title and Crossref metadata only - enrichment should verify.

items.title: Commercial multimodal large language models show systematic model-specific errors in breast cancer pathology reporting: a paired concordance study
items.excerpt: Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-5.5 were each given 16 H&E tiles per case for 427 invasive breast cancers and compared against a board-certified breast pathologist on Nottingham grade and receptor-defined subtype; each model showed systematic, model-specific errors.

items.title: Opinion: AI depends on medical records that don't always tell the full truth about women
items.excerpt: Doctors often disregard women's complaints and symptoms, so clinical AI is trained on medical records that are incorrect - a bias problem for AI diagnosis in pain and mental health.

items.title: New Study Shows Benefits of AI Analysis for Ultrasound Reports and Incidental Findings of Hepatic Steatosis
items.excerpt: Gadi Lalazar, MD, discusses research showing natural language processing improves recognition of incidental hepatic steatosis in ultrasound reports, so findings that radiologists mention are not lost before follow-up.

items.title: CCTA Study: AI-Powered Plaque Analysis Reveals Coronary Plaque in 87 Percent of Retired NFL Players
items.excerpt: AI plaque analysis of coronary CT angiography found plaque in 87% of retired NFL players and severe or extensive total plaque volume in 27%, according to a study presented at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026.

items.title: FDA Clears AI-Enabled Chest CT Software for Aortic Analysis
items.excerpt: FDA cleared Coreline Soft's AVIEW Aorta Metrics, which automatically segments aortic regions and classifies aortic zones on chest CT images.

items.title: AI-powered urine test distinguishes bladder disorders with up to 92% accuracy
items.excerpt: Asan Medical Center researchers developed an AI urine-testing technique that distinguishes interstitial cystitis, overactive bladder and healthy individuals with up to 92% accuracy, helping separate conditions with overlapping symptoms.
